static_traits.name: Wang Ailin
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive friends and family to confide in, but has not yet communicated with them about this specific difficulty; some tension arises with friends of different preferences due to sports preferences, and enjoyment at social gatherings has decreased
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no history of psychotherapy or treatment for psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to recognize and describe own negative thinking patterns; tone slightly nervous but highly cooperative, able to self-reflect

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to label myself as 'having no taste in sports' because I prefer baseball to football. This thinking leads to self-criticism and doubt about my own preferences.
basic_info.core_demands: These negative thoughts have affected my enjoyment of sports and brought unnecessary stress, so I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: In high school, peers generally were enthusiastic about football rather than baseball; because my preference differed, I felt out of place and at risk of being excluded. From then on I formed a habit of self-labeling ('no taste in sports', 'so strange'), and repeatedly experienced guilt and embarrassment in social situations involving discussing sports or watching games; to conform to social and group expectations, I once tried to change my preference to match the majority, but did not succeed, and this continued into adulthood over the long term.

special_situations.event: When discussing football (such as the Super Bowl) with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not like football, it means I have no taste in sports / am abnormal, and I will be seen as weird
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding sports topics or pretending to like American football more to cater to others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I must be very strange / I have no taste in sports

special_situations.event: At a social gathering watching a sports match, people around generally prefer American football
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should stay consistent with everyone, liking American football is what counts as 'normal'
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forces oneself to pay attention to American football and cater to mainstream views
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should like football like everyone else

special_situations.event: Recalling the high school environment where peers generally loved American football
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Being different from the majority means not being accepted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism and trying to change preferences to gain acceptance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not like football, which shows I do not fit in

special_situations.event: When talking about sports with friends, presuming others will evaluate one's preferences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express real preferences, I will be looked down on or thought to be very strange
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Changing the subject, avoiding discussion of sports
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am strange / look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted, able to freely and authentically express one's sports interests
core_conflict.fear: Fears being judged, humiliated, or excluded by the group, becoming 'the person who does not fit in'
defense_goal: Avoiding rejection by catering to others' preferences and suppressing oneself
Avoids talking about sports to reduce the anxiety of exposure

object_relations.self_representation: An outsider who is different from others and easily negated
object_relations.object_representation: Picky judges / a group that divides worth by mainstream preferences

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing football or the Super Bowl with friends and others express strong mainstream preferences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes that if they do not follow the crowd they will be seen as 'strange' and relationships will be damaged (attributing judgmental intentions to others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses an accommodating tone, emphasizing that they 'also like rugby', avoiding revealing true interests; agrees with others' views as much as possible to maintain harmony.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When directly asked about the favorite sport or invited to talk about personal preferences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Presumes the other person will look down on or negate them, feeling that expressing true preferences equals being rejected
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Evades deeper exchange by changing the topic, self-mockery, or downplaying; cautious tone, avoids clearly expressing a stance.

manifestations: Feels that social expectations require him to conform to mainstream sports preferences
Uses 'should' statements to demand that he like football
Experiences guilt and embarrassment when expressing true interests
Felt out of place in high school due to different preferences
Worries about being looked down on or excluded by friends
outcomes: Tends to pretend to conform to avoid being isolated

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently labels himself ('no taste in sports', 'so strange') and criticizes himself
Overly cautious when talking about sports, worrying that his expressions will be judged

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Proactively changes the topic or avoids detailed discussion when talking about sports with friends
Avoids expressing true interests in social settings

contact_model.definition: The individual's boundaries between self and others or groups are unclear, with a tendency toward sameness, dissolving individual awareness, corresponding to 'withdrawal'.
manifestations: Pretends to like football more in order to stay consistent with the group
Forces himself to conform to mainstream preferences

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'
manifestations: Presupposes that others will look down on him or think he is 'strange'
Attributes judgment to friends without verification

positive_force: Having a supportive network of friends and family (though this specific trouble has not been shared)
Willing to seek psychological counseling and try behavioral experiments
Able to identify and name their own cognitive distortions (such as all-or-nothing thinking, overgeneralization, mind reading, and 'should' statements)
Maintains a steady interest and motivation in sports (a sports enthusiast)
Work performance unaffected, basic functioning good
negative_force: Social conformity pressure and external evaluation orientation (seeking external validation)
Avoiding and people-pleasing when talking about sports, compromising authenticity
Guilt and embarrassment occur frequently, increasing stress
Strained relationships with friends whose preferences differ

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding talking about sports topics or changing the topic
antecedent: When discussing sports/the Super Bowl with friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about not being accepted and being judged, tending to seek external recognition to reduce anxiety
target_behavior.function: Escaping being evaluated and embarrassment, maintaining superficial harmony of group relationships
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased pleasure in sports activities, social unease, worsening relationship tension

target_behavior.behavior: Pretending to like football more to fit in with the group
antecedent: When friends strongly express preference for American football or expect agreement
When directly asked about one's favorite sport
target_behavior.core_reason: Believes only by being consistent with the majority can one be accepted, fearing being labeled 'weird / tasteless'
target_behavior.function: Gaining group acceptance and recognition, reducing the risk of exclusion
target_behavior.consequence: Authenticity is compromised, self-doubt deepens, and long-term stress increases
